title: Gyoza
subtitle: Japanese pork and cabbage potsticker dumplings
excerpt: Gyoza are Japanese potsticker dumplings: a thin wheat wrapper filled with pork mince, cabbage, and ginger, then pan-fried until the base is crisp and steamed under a lid to cook the top. They are served with a dipping sauce of soy sauce and rice vinegar.
sourceNotes: Gyoza are derived from the Chinese jiaozi but evolved their own distinct Japanese form: thinner wrappers, a stronger garlic and sesame flavour, and the characteristic crisp-bottomed pan-frying method (yaki-gyoza) with a small amount of water to steam under a lid. They became popular in Japan after World War II.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze raw gyoza on a baking tray, then transfer to a bag. Cook from frozen: increase steaming time by 2 to 3 minutes.
recipe.batchNotes: This recipe makes about 24 gyoza. Scale up in direct proportion. Make a large batch and freeze half.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The filling keeps in the fridge for up to 24 hours. Assemble and cook when ready.

content.text: The filling must be squeezed completely dry before use. Wet filling makes the wrapper soggy and prevents a crisp base. Squeeze the salted cabbage in a clean cloth or your hands until no more moisture comes out. The pleating takes practice: for a beginner, pinch the edges together in 3 to 4 folds on one side; it does not need to be perfect to taste good.

items.prepNote: 2 tbsp for the filling, 3 tbsp for the dipping sauce

content.text: Toss the shredded cabbage with a pinch of salt and leave for 10 minutes. Squeeze out as much water as possible in a clean cloth or with your hands.

Mix the pork mince, drained cabbage, spring onion, ginger, garlic, soy sauce, and sesame oil together. Stir vigorously in one direction for 1 to 2 minutes until the mixture becomes slightly sticky and pasty. This improves the texture.

Place a gyoza wrapper on a clean surface. Put 1 teaspoon of filling in the centre. Dampen the edge of the wrapper with water. Fold in half to form a semicircle. Pleat the front edge in 3 to 4 folds, pressing firmly against the flat back edge to seal. Place seam-side up on a floured tray.

Heat the sunflower oil in a large non-stick frying pan over medium-high heat. Place the gyoza flat-side down in a single layer (cook in batches if needed). Cook without moving for 2 to 3 minutes until the bases are golden brown.

Pour 100 ml of water into the pan (it will spit), cover immediately with a lid, and steam for 4 to 5 minutes until the water has evaporated and the tops are cooked through. Remove the lid and let any remaining water evaporate for 1 minute. Serve immediately with dipping sauce.

items.symptom: Gyoza stick to the pan and the bases tear when serving
items.cause: Pan not hot enough before the gyoza went in, or not enough oil
items.fix: The oil must be shimmering hot before the gyoza go in. Once placed, do not move them until the base has set. Use a thin palette knife to release them gently.

items.symptom: Wrappers are soggy and the filling is wet
items.cause: Cabbage was not squeezed dry enough
items.fix: This is the most common failure. After salting and resting, the cabbage must be squeezed until almost dry. Wet filling defeats the purpose of the crispy-bottom cooking method.
